interleukin-6 strongly stimulates hepatic insulin like growth factor binding protein 4 (IGFBP-4) messenger RNA and protein levels in vitro and in rat liver in vivo.
IL-6 is a potent stimulator of hepatic IGFB-4 gene expression in vitro and in vitro.
IL-6 induces hepatic IGFBPs-4 gene expression in vitro and in rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which cytokines and glucocoicoids regulate hepatic insulin-like binding protein (IGFBP)-4 gene expression and secretion.
the effects of proinflammatory cytokine IL-6, and glucocorticoid dexamethasome, on IGFBP gene expression in primary cultured hepatocytes.
the role of the cytokines in the regulation of IGFs and their binding proteins in the liver and in the whole animal, and the mechanisms by which these cytokines act.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IL-6 is the major mediator of IGFBP4 induction in liver and in serum.
IL-6 is a potent inducer of IGFBP4 in liver, whereas glucocorticoids are not able to modulate IGFBP4 gene expression and protein production.
IL-6 induces hepatic IGFBPs-1 and -4, whereas glucocorticoids and TNF-alpha decrease IGFBP-3 and IGFBP-rP1 and IL-1ss decreases IGFBP-5.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IL-6, IL-1ss, and TNF-alpha have a direct effect on IGFBPs and that glucocorticoids can modulate this effect.
